title: "Impact"

---

Research reaches a decision or it does not. These are the places where it has.

## Policy tools in public use

[eMANDEVAL](/tools/emandeval/) takes preference estimates for vaccine mandate
design and makes them comparable across designs, so that a policymaker weighing
options can see which combinations retain public support. [STEPS](/tools/steps/)
does the same for field-epidemiology training scale-up, on a cost model and choice
experiment developed for a World Bank business case. The [farming benefit–cost
tool](/tools/soil-crc-bca/) applies the approach to soil and farming
interventions.

## A literature made usable

The COVID-19 vaccine mandate evidence was spread across epidemiology, economics,
political science and public health, in formats that did not compare. The [open
repository](/research/data-and-code/) collects it, with a worked scoping review of
the quasi-experimental studies, and is maintained so others can extend it rather
than rebuild it.

## Advising and review

Guest Editor for *Health Policy and Technology*. Reviewer for the *Journal of
Health Economics*, *Health Economics*, *Value in Health*, *Social Science &
Medicine*, the *Journal of Choice Modelling*, *Theory and Decision* and *BMJ Open*.
